article_lead.description: a predictor that combines several fitted models so their differing errors can partly cancel or be corrected

new_bank_questions.title: Correlation in an ensemble average
new_bank_questions.body: Four numerical predictors have error variance 1 each and pairwise correlation 0.5. Find the variance of their average under this equal-correlation model.
new_bank_questions.answer: It is 0.5+(1-0.5)/4=0.625. The independent case would give 0.25; common error does not disappear as the ensemble grows.

new_bank_questions.title: Voting is not averaging labels
new_bank_questions.body: Three classifiers predict category labels A, A and B. What is the plurality result, and why does the numerical squared-error identity for a mean not prove anything about this vote?
new_bank_questions.answer: A wins with two votes. Category names are not numerical values, and zero-one classification loss after a vote is not squared loss of an average.

new_bank_questions.title: How members differ
new_bank_questions.body: Contrast the mechanism making members different in bagging, a random forest, and AdaBoost.
new_bank_questions.answer: Bagging fits the base learner to bootstrap resamples. A random forest adds random candidate-variable choices at tree splits. AdaBoost sequentially changes training-example weights to emphasize difficult cases and combines weighted learners.
